purpose: Discover the exact pinned-runtime instruction path that reinitializes a lost level by watching the anchored Board's low-frequency score-target field for writes, instead of guessing a reset function entry.

trigger.finding: The natural-loss sequence completed and changed target 9650 to 9616 on the same Board, but candidate entry 0x00419A90 had zero hits. A field watchpoint is required to identify the actual writer without another entry guess.

frozen_data_watchpoint.trigger_semantics: x86 data breakpoint is observed after the writing instruction completes

required: post-instruction EIP and debug exception address
32-byte code window centered around the post-instruction EIP
active Board address, native time, score, score target, and curve-plan-exhausted flag
previous observed score target and post-write score target

allowed: Add a board_global_precall_and_target_write trace kind to the existing tracer and recorder.
Add an explicit DR0 four-byte write-watchpoint retarget helper and deterministic tests for its DR7 encoding and restoration.
After the source anchor, compute the watched address only from that run's source Board plus the frozen 0x108 offset.
Collect no more than sixteen writes and stop on the first positive target different from the source target.
Reuse verified-foreground navigation and exact source-anchor monitor derivation.
forbidden: Any process-memory write, software breakpoint, gameplay action, swap, fruit shot, or post-output target selection.
Changing the natural-loss v3 predicate or provenance validator before c153 output.
Treating a timeout, score-target change without the data watchpoint, or a static candidate address as c153 PASS.
Fidelity Gate credit, Training Gate credit, or training start from c153.

decision_rule.pass: Retain c153a1 and freeze a separate exact writer/call-path semantic protocol from the observed post-EIP, stack, and Board state before implementation or formal source recording.
decision_rule.fail: Retain c153a1 and localize the first structural failure without retry-selection or threshold weakening.
